title: Immutable State Compatibility Layer for priv EKS Terraform Module
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: our existing priv EKS Terraform module assumes a single centralized TF state and uses destructive replace operations during control-plane upgrades. This makes zero-downtime upgrades and safe on-prem migrations risky for customers with strict RTO/RPO. Goal: build an immutable-state compatibility layer (a thin Terraform wrapper + orchestration guide) that enables safe transitions from our old state layout to a per-cluster immutable state model without service disruption, and enforces pre-apply health checks and plan-time safety gates.
background: We continue to see incidents where control plane upgrades or certificate rotations trigger transient API server unavailability during terraform apply. Previous tickets focused on preflight checks and upgrade orchestration, but we need a reusable module-level shim that encodes best-practices (import helpers, guarded apply, canary plan, rollout window checks) so downstream customer IaC remains simple. This work should be compatible with both Hosted-private and on-prem deploys.
proposed_solution:
1) Add a compat wrapper module (terraform module: rw_priv_controlplane_compat) which: - supports dual-state import helpers to map resources from legacy state to per-cluster state files. - exposes 'safe_apply' boolean and 'canary_ratio' to run canary nodegroup/control-plane changes first. - implements plan-time validation (checks for disruptive changes such as api-server replacement, kube-apiserver cert rotation, and kms key replacement) and fails the apply unless 'force' is set with explicit justification.
2) Provide a small operator (stateless Lambda or container in private control plane) that can run post-apply health probes (kube-apiserver readiness, KMS decrypt test, operator CR health) and report back to a dedicated rollout dashboard.
3) Include a documented migration playbook with import commands and rollback recipes and add automated sanity checks to the Terraform pipeline (CI gate).
acceptance_criteria: Module published to terraform registry under rw_priv_controlplane_compat with semantic versioning
Can perform non-destructive migration: import legacy control-plane resources into new per-cluster state without downtime in staging environment
Plan-time blockers prevent apply for high-risk changes unless explicit approval is given
Automated post-apply healthcheck returns green within defined SLOs (api-server ready < 2m, KMS decrypt < 500ms) in 95% of runs
CI pipeline includes a dry-run that exercises the canary flow and blocks on health regressions

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: State import mistakes could orphan resources. Mitigation: provide 'preview-import' that runs a dry-run and outputs exact terraform import commands and checks resource hashes before changes.
Risk: Plan-time validators may produce false-positives. Mitigation: maintain an allowlist and add a two-step approval with automated justification logging.
Risk: Post-apply checks introduce additional permissions surface. Mitigation: use least-privilege IAM roles and scoped short-lived credentials for health runner.

rollback_strategy: If a migration attempt causes unexpected resource disruption, we will: 1) Halt further applies, 2) Re-import previous state snapshot into TF state, 3) Trigger automated remediation playbook (restore kubeadmin certs and reattach nodegroups), 4) Open incident and run postmortem. All steps documented in runbook.
notes: Aim is to provide this as an opt-in compatibility layer for customers migrating from older templates. Downstream infra teams will be able to adopt the module incrementally. Keep module surface intentionally small and extensively tested.
